title: The Due column reads 1 day and ordinal days correctly for the shop's terms
custom_preconds:
Preconditions

  • Sign in as an Admin at the test location.
  • Make sure the shop has its own active terms: term A due 1 day after the invoice date, term B due 365 days after, and day-of-the-following-month terms C (day 1), D (day 2), E (day 3), F (day 11), G (day 12), H (day 13), J (day 21), K (day 22), L (day 23) and M (day 31).
  • Start on the Credit Terms page (Settings, then "Credit Terms" in the Finance group), Active tab.
custom_steps: 1. Read the Due column for term A to term M.
custom_expected:
Expected Result

Step 1:

  • Term A reads "1 day after the invoice date" (singular).
  • Term B reads "365 days after the invoice date"
  • Term C "1st of the following month", term D "2nd of the following month", term E "3rd of the following month", term F "11th of the following month", term G "12th of the following month", term H "13th of the following month", term J "21st of the following month", term K "22nd of the following month", term L "23rd of the following month", term M "31st of the following month".

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

From: PRD "Credit terms", Confluence 963346440, version 3 (22 Oct 2026, "Renamed to Credit terms", Chris Ward), read 23 Oct 2026 · Epic SV-11638, story SV-11670 (Story 1, Credit Terms page and list)

  • S1-R7: “The Due column describes each term in words:”
  • S1-R7, a Net term: “A Net term: "{X} days after the invoice date" ("1 day after the invoice date" when X is 1), for example "30 days after the invoice date"”
  • S1-R7, a day of the following month term: “A "day of the following month" term: "{ordinal day} of the following month", for example "10th of the following month", "1st of the following month", "22nd of the following month"”
  • Key Decisions: “Net terms run from 1 to 365 days.”

The build is not yet available to check this case against.
